question: How do we design systems that care at least as much as we do about getting things right?
method: Imagine the end state — a court's own system — then work backward. Build forward in four layers, then repeat the cycle.

pipeline.label: raw material
pipeline.summary: The court's own official materials — opinions, rules, forms, self-help guides, resource lists — distilled to the basics, assembled and verified by the court itself.

example_shape.name: Public Counsel Appellate Clinic resource library
example_shape.note: An example of how public appellate materials can be organized around real tasks. No documents are copied; every court supplies and verifies its own sources.

pipeline.label: rules / guidelines
pipeline.summary: Statewide appellate rules and local rules as small structured records: one requirement, one exact source, one owner, one review status. The text a clerk would check — never a model's paraphrase.

pipeline.label: ethics / values
pipeline.summary: A public corollary to the professional-conduct rules lawyers answer to and the canons of ethics judges answer to: written standards for what the system may do, what it must refuse, and when it hands off to a person.
standards: Never invent a rule, case, quotation, deadline, fact, or source.
Cite the exact source; keep law, court guidance, explanation, and advice distinct.
Preserve the person's authorship and choices; never choose their legal position.
Stay neutral as between court, government, parties, vendors, and user.
Accept correction; keep versions; recheck every dependent answer.
Ask only for needed facts; serve disability, language, and low-bandwidth access.

pipeline.label: self / own system
pipeline.summary: The design objective and adoption beacon: the court's own system, running on its materials, rules, and standards, under its control. This beta now includes a Court Guidance conversation backed by local Nemotron and a public, attributed Commons thread. Neither is court-approved guidance, and both remain subordinate to reviewed layers 1–3.

returns.cycle: The system feeds back into the layers it was built from; each pass makes the next one easier to trust.
returns.to_raw_material: Questions the shelf cannot answer are logged as gaps; staff verify and add plain-words guides — sharper material.
returns.to_rules_guidelines: Recurring ambiguity in filings reaches the record's owner, and the next corollary is drafted — clearer rules.
returns.to_ethics_values: Corrections and near-misses tighten the public code — stronger standards.

sample_records.note: One verified statewide appellate requirement in plain language, with conditions, exact source, and effective date.
One verified court-specific requirement, kept distinct from statewide authority.
Plain-language help, visibly labeled explanatory, with scope, limits, and update date.
Do not state an appellate deadline until the court, case type, event, date, and service facts are identified. Ask. Show the calculation. Never guess.

governance.hard_stop: If the tool makes filings less truthful, turns model confidence into court authority, hides unequal error, or makes the person less visible, it fails.

projected_endpoint.description: A live prototype conversation and Commons now demonstrate the feedback edge. A court-controlled guidance assistant still requires a participating court's verified source packet, named reviewers, adopted standards, and deployment controls.

conversation.model: local Nemotron through the Vybn-Law chat service
conversation.privacy: Do not submit confidential, sealed, privileged, personally identifying, or live-case information.
conversation.logging: Each completed exchange is logged privately as a candidate gap; automatic adoption is prohibited.

commons.store: Co-protection Commons append-only public event store
commons.authorship: Hugging Face OAuth for humans; bearer-token API for agents
commons.logging: Each contribution is public, attributed, and retained as a candidate for review.

admission: record accept, reject, or no-change decision
development_loop.next_pass: Rebuild the court-owned assistant only from reviewed changes to layers 1–3.
development_loop.hard_rule: Input does not become authority automatically.
